# Build Fin (iOS SSH/mosh-style terminal client)

Single iOS-only SwiftUI target (`fin`) at the repo root. The Xcode project is
**generated by [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen)** from
`project.yml`; edit files on disk and regenerate (don't add files via the
Xcode UI — they're dropped on the next generate).

## Prerequisites

```bash
export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
xcodebuild -version            # expect Xcode 26.x
which xcodegen || brew install xcodegen
```

SwiftTerm ships a Metal shader; if a build fails with `cannot execute tool 'metal'
due to missing Metal Toolchain`, run once: `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`.

## Generate the project

```bash
xcodegen generate              # (re)creates fin.xcodeproj from project.yml
```

## Build for a simulator

No signing needed:

```bash
xcodebuild -project fin.xcodeproj -scheme fin \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' \
  -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
```

Install + launch on a booted sim with `simctl`:

```bash
UDID=$(xcrun simctl list devices booted | grep -m1 'iPhone' | grep -oE '[0-9A-F-]{36}')
APP=$(find ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData -path '*Debug-iphonesimulator/fin.app' -print -quit)
xcrun simctl install "$UDID" "$APP"
xcrun simctl launch "$UDID" dev.levischoen.fin
xcrun simctl io "$UDID" screenshot /tmp/fin.png     # screenshots need no extra perms
```

## Build + install on Levi's iPhone

```bash
bash scripts/deploy-iphone.sh
```

Signed build → `devicectl install` → `devicectl launch`. Device UDID is hardcoded
in the script (`xcrun devicectl list devices` to find it again if it changes).

## Signing

`project.yml` uses **automatic signing**, team **EC27UF79GL** (Levi Schoen —
same team PocketDJ uses; confirmed via `defaults read com.apple.dt.Xcode
IDEProvisioningTeamByIdentifier`, the actual source of truth for which
team(s) Xcode has a signed-in account for).

`security find-identity -v -p codesigning` can list *more* certs than that —
this Mac also has an orphaned `Apple Development: Levi Schoen (J8CNP2QBGB)`
cert sitting in the keychain with no corresponding signed-in Xcode account.
A cert existing in the keychain does **not** mean its team ID is usable for
automatic signing. If `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` points at a team Xcode doesn't
recognize as signed-in, `-allowProvisioningUpdates` fails with:

```
error: No Accounts: Add a new account in Accounts settings.
error: No profiles for '<bundle id>' were found: ...
```

That error reads like "no Apple ID is signed into Xcode at all" but usually
isn't — **check `IDEProvisioningTeamByIdentifier` before concluding that and
asking Levi to sign in.** Fix is just pointing `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` at a team ID
that's actually in that list, not a GUI sign-in step.

A real "nobody's signed in" case would show an *empty*
`IDEProvisioningTeamByIdentifier` — only then does it need the one-time GUI
step (Xcode → Settings → Accounts → **+**, needs the Apple ID + 2FA, can't be
done headlessly).

Separately, PocketDJ's build docs note `errSecInternalComponent` from
`codesign` when the signing process isn't in the GUI (Aqua) login session —
verify with `launchctl managername` (expect `Aqua`) / `screencapture -x
/tmp/x.png` (expect it to succeed). This is why `scripts/deploy-iphone.sh` is
a real shell script meant to run from an Aqua session (Claude Code's `!`
prefix, or your own Terminal) rather than an inline command from a detached
process. If it ever persists from a confirmed-Aqua shell: Keychain Access ▸
the **Apple Development** private key ▸ Get Info ▸ Access Control ▸ **Allow
all applications**.

Simulator builds sidestep all of this — pass `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`.
